name: Code, Prose
need: The system is being asked to render its own documentation, and it turns out to have no documentation-shaped parts. Measured while building the site: 181 lines of hand-written CSS across 37 classes, of which roughly half were flex stacks that <Stack>, <Row> and <Grid> already cover — a discovery failure on the agent's side, now fixed — and the rest split into three things the registry genuinely does not have. A system that cannot describe itself in its own parts is a real gap, and it is the gap every consumer hits the moment they write a README page, an empty-state explanation or a settings hint.

consideredAlternatives.whyNot: Covers the stacking and is now used for it. It does not set a measure, a reading colour or a monospace context, which is what the three below are for.
Covers the surface an example is shown on and the code block's frame; it says nothing about the text inside them.
Kbd is one key, Highlight is a matched substring, Quote is an attributed passage. None is a block of code or a paragraph of body text.
That is the status quo and it is what this request measured: every app writes the same muted paragraph at the same measure, and gets the measure slightly different each time.

proposedApi.Code: children (the source), inline (a fragment in a sentence vs a block), language (labelling only, no highlighting in v1), copy (renders the existing <CopyButton>). Monospace face, the system's own scroll contract for anything wide — a code block that reflows lies about the code.
proposedApi.Prose: children, size (sm | md), tone (default | muted), as (p | div). One job: body text at a MEASURE. The measure is the whole reason it exists — 68ch was arrived at independently in four files while writing the site.

sources: The system's own site, built 2026-08-23. Every documentation system that exists ships these (Primer, Polaris, Carbon, Material all have a code block and a text/prose primitive); this one shipped 126 components without them because it had never been asked to explain itself.
decision: Code and Prose approved and built 2026-08-23 — a system that cannot describe itself in its own parts is a real gap, and both shipped the same day. The decision was never written here, so the folder claimed for three days that the system was waiting on a call already made; the check that should have said so read the batch name as one phrase and found no registry file called "Code, Prose, ColorSwatch" (fixed 2026-08-26). ColorSwatch was neither built nor decided and is not a documentation part at all — it is a colour CONTROL. Split out as its own request rather than carried along by a batch it only ever shared a day with.
decidedBy: owner (2026-08-26, told the pending requests to be worked)
